subject: Re: Security & Subprocessors - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security & Subprocessors - follow-up from today's call

Hi Daniel / Alicia 	6

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on compliance and third-party risk items: 

1) SOC 2: you asked about our compliance posture. We are currently SOC 2 Type II in progress; our timeline for the latest audit report (covering Jan-Dec 2025) is end of Q2 2026. I can share the SOC 2 bridge letter and interim controls summary once the audit accountants release them.

2) GDPR / HIPAA scope: per our call, your use case is PII processing for EU customers and potential PHI for a subset of records. We'll need to confirm the following to scope controls and DPA language:
   - Data flows (which fields are sent to the API)
   - Retention & deletion expectations
   - Whether you need a HIPAA BAA for the PHI portion (we can support BAA for covered workloads).

3) Subprocessors: I attached our canonical subprocessor list snapshot (see attachments) and highlighted the core cloud providers (AWS/GCP), analytics providers, and our telemetry/monitoring vendors. Please review and flag any vendors that require additional evidence.

4) Vendor questionnaire: I can fill your security questionnaire or we can share a completed copy of our standard vendor security packet (SOC/QSA contact, encryption, incident process, penetration test summaries). If you prefer, upload your questionnaire and we'll return a completed copy within 3 business days.

Next steps / asks:
- Daniel: please confirm whether you want a full questionnaire response or the standard packet.
- Alicia: can you share the specific data fields you expect to send (or a sample schema) so we can confirm processing boundaries for GDPR/HIPAA?
- We will share the subprocessor PDF and the questionnaire stub within this thread.

I'll loop in Rishi (SE) and Vivek (security) for any technical/security clarifications.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_q1_2026.pdf (stub)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security & Subprocessors - follow-up from today's call

Thanks Marissa 	6 helpful summary. A few notes from our side: 

- SOC 2: we will need at minimum a SOC 2 Type II report (or a bridge letter + attestation timeline) before procurement can sign off. Is your SOC 2 scoped to hosting/processing only or does it include your managed services?

- GDPR / HIPAA: we'll provide a sample schema by end of day tomorrow. For HIPAA, we will likely need a signed BAA for the PHI scope 	6 can you confirm if Redwood has a standard BAA?

- Subprocessors: please send the canonical list (we'll compare against our third-party inventory). If any subprocessors have cross-border transfer implications, call those out. Also let us know which vendors have access to raw request payloads versus aggregated telemetry.

Appreciate it 	6 looking forward to the questionnaire or packet.

Daniel
CTO, Acme Corp
daniel.park@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-16T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security & Subprocessors - next steps

Great, thanks Daniel. Attaching the subprocessor snapshot and a partially completed copy of your questionnaire (we filled the vendor-side fields to speed review).

Quick clarifications inline:
- SOC 2 scope: our SOC 2 covers Redwood's hosted API and control plane, including the infrastructure layers used to serve requests (we work with AWS and GCP as primary cloud providers). Managed services or professional services engagements are not automatically in scope 	6 if you expect Redwood to process PHI under a managed services arrangement, let's flag that so we can extend coverage or document compensating controls.

- Cross-border transfers: our subprocessor list notes data residency wherever applicable. For EU data, we offer options to pin requests to EU regions; otherwise, requests may be routed to nearest compatible region depending on your account configuration. The attached PDF calls out which subprocessors store backups or have access to logs.

- Access to raw payloads: only a small set of internal roles and our logging vendor have access to raw request payloads in rare troubleshooting scenarios. Telemetry/analytics are aggregated and pseudonymized. Vivek can add a note with vendor-level access details.

Requested next steps: 
1) Send us your sample schema (Alicia) 	6 we'll confirm processing boundaries and update the DPA/BAA language if needed.
2) If you want a completed questionnaire, please re-upload the latest version to the Drive link below; we'll return within 3 business days.
3) Let us know any subprocessors you'd like additional evidence for (pen test reports, vendor attestations).

Drive link for uploads: https://drive.redwood.com/s/ACME-Vendor-Questionnaire

Thanks 	6 looping Vivek for the vendor access detail.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_vendor_questionnaire_filled.xlsx (stub), redwood_subprocessors_q1_2026.pdf (stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecorp.com>; Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security & Subprocessors - next steps

Hi Daniel / Alicia 	6

Following up with a few vendor-level clarifications: 

- Cloud providers: AWS (primary compute + S3 backups), GCP (analytics workloads for one EU region tenant). Both are engaged under business associate agreements where required and we maintain customer-specific region pinning for EU-only deployments.

- Raw payload access: Limited to on-call engineers (as part of incident triage) and our logging vendor (LogSight) under strict role-based access. Access requires approval via our ticketing system and is logged; we retain access logs for 24 months.

- Encryption: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is provider-managed CMKs for most storage 	6 we support bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) for dedicated/private deployments.

If you need: 
- A redacted pen test summary (we can provide)
- Our interim SOC 2 controls summary (bridge letter) 	6 expected by end of Q2 2026
- A draft BAA: we have a standard template and can provide a version marked for DE-IDENTIFIED PHI or FULL PHI processing depending on your requirements.

I'll attach the subprocessor PDF and the completed questionnaire we started. If you'd like a quick >15 minute call to run through any of the items, Marissa can coordinate.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
